title: google-gemini/gemini-cli — An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal.
content:
Note
Unpaid tier and Google One users: Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18th, 2026. To learn more, see our blog post.
Gemini CLI has not been optimized for Gemini 4 Argon. To use Gemini 4 Argon, please use Antigravity.
Note
Gemini CLI is not optimized for the latest Gemini models. For the best coding experience with Gemini models use Antigravity CLI
Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal. It provides lightweight access to Gemini, giving you the most direct path from your prompt to our model.
Learn all about Gemini CLI in our documentation.
See Gemini CLI installation, execution, and releases for recommended system specifications and a detailed installation guide.
# Using npx (no installation required)
npx @google/gemini-clinpm install -g @google/gemini-clibrew install gemini-clisudo port install gemini-cli# Create and activate a new environment
conda create -y -n gemini_env -c conda-forge nodejs
conda activate gemini_env
# Install Gemini CLI globally via npm (inside the environment)
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
See Releases for more details.
New preview releases will be published each week at UTC 23:59 on Tuesdays. These
releases will not have been fully vetted and may contain regressions or other
outstanding issues. Please help us test and install with preview tag.
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@preview
- New stable releases will be published each week at UTC 20:00 on Tuesdays, this
will be the full promotion of last week's preview release + any bug fixes
and validations. Use latest tag.
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@latest
- New releases will be published each day at UTC 00:00. This will be all changes
from the main branch as represented at time of release. It should be assumed
there are pending validations and issues. Use nightly tag.
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@nightly
- Query and edit large codebases
- Generate new apps from PDFs, images, or sketches using multimodal capabilities
- Debug issues and troubleshoot with natural language
- Automate operational tasks like querying pull requests or handling complex rebases
- Use MCP servers to connect new capabilities, including media generation with Imagen, Veo or Lyria
- Run non-interactively in scripts for workflow automation
Choose the authentication method that best fits your needs:
When using a paid Code Assist License from your organization, remember to set the Google Cloud Project
# Set your Google Cloud Project
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
gemini
✨ Best for: Developers who need specific model control or paid tier access
Benefits:
- Model selection: Choose specific Gemini models
- Usage-based billing: Upgrade for higher limits when needed
# Get your key from https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
gemini
✨ Best for: Enterprise teams and production workloads
Benefits:
- Enterprise features: Advanced security and compliance
- Scalable: Higher rate limits with billing account
- Integration: Works with existing Google Cloud infrastructure
# Get your key from Google Cloud Console
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true
gemini
For Google Workspace accounts and other authentication methods, see the authentication guide.
Note
Gemini CLI is not optimized for the latest Gemini models. For the best coding experience with Gemini models use Antigravity CLI
geminigemini --include-directories ../lib,../docsgemini -m gemini-2.5-flash
Get a simple text response:
gemini -p "Explain the architecture of this codebase"
For more advanced scripting, including how to parse JSON and handle errors, use
the --output-format json flag to get structured output:
gemini -p "Explain the architecture of this codebase" --output-format json
For real-time event streaming (useful for monitoring long-running operations),
use --output-format stream-json to get newline-delimited JSON events:
gemini -p "Run tests and deploy" --output-format stream-jsoncd new-project/
gemini

report.summary: Google's open-source Gemini CLI put a Gemini agent in the terminal, but Google now redirects unpaid users to Antigravity CLI for newer models.
report.background: Terminal-based coding agents became one of the most contested fronts in AI development after Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex CLI and open-source rivals like Aider showed that developers would rather delegate work to an agent that lives where they already work — the shell — than switch to a new editor. Google responded with Gemini CLI, an Apache 2.0 project that wrapped Gemini models in a single installable command, paired it with a generous free authentication path through a Google account, and let it read, edit and reason over large repositories. The project became a flagship for Google's developer outreach and one of the most-starred agent repositories on GitHub. The notice now atop the repo marks a second phase: Google is consolidating its agent strategy around Antigravity, and the terminal tool is being repositioned rather than retired outright.
key_points: Installation is deliberately frictionless: `npx @google/gemini-cli` runs it with no installation at all, while npm, Homebrew, MacPorts and conda cover persistent setups. Releases follow three channels — nightly builds daily at 00:00 UTC, preview builds Tuesday evenings, and a stable 'latest' tag promoted the following week — letting teams choose between bleeding edge and vetted code.

Capabilities go well beyond chat. The agent queries and edits large codebases, generates new applications from PDFs, images or sketches using Gemini's multimodal input, debugs in natural language, and automates operational chores like listing pull requests or untangling complex rebases. MCP servers plug in external tools, including media generation through Imagen, Veo and Lyria.

Authentication splits three ways: an organisational Code Assist licence tied to a Google Cloud project, a personal Gemini API key from AI Studio for model selection and usage-based billing, or Vertex AI credentials for enterprise workloads needing compliance, higher rate limits and existing cloud integration. One binary thus serves hobbyists, teams and regulated enterprises under very different billing and governance models.

The tool is built to be scripted, not just typed into. The -p flag sends a one-shot prompt, --output-format json returns structured results for pipelines, and stream-json emits newline-delimited events for monitoring long-running jobs. Context files (GEMINI.md), custom slash commands, checkpointing, token caching and sandboxed execution make it viable inside CI and ops automation.

The repository now leads with a redirect: since 18 June 2026, unpaid-tier and Google One users were moved to Antigravity CLI, and Gemini CLI is explicitly stated as 'not optimized' for the newest Gemini models, including Gemini 4 Argon. The code stays Apache 2.0 with community contributions still welcome, but Google's recommended path for best coding results is now a different product.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the notice is a case study in how quickly open-source flagships can be repositioned when model generations shift. Shipping a CLI is cheap; keeping it aligned with each new model's tooling and prompt behaviour is not, and Google has chosen to concentrate that effort in Antigravity rather than maintain parallel surfaces. For developers, the practical consequence is migration work: MCP server configurations in ~/.gemini/settings.json, GEMINI.md context files, custom commands and shell scripts built around -p and --output-format must be re-validated against a new binary. The Apache 2.0 licence softens the blow — anyone can fork or self-host — but teams that standardised on the CLI for automation now carry a portability risk they should factor into tooling decisions. For regular users, the free on-ramp through a personal Google account is the part that changed most visibly.
report.tools: Watch Antigravity CLI as the successor surface, and the Model Context Protocol ecosystem, since MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, database connectors, Imagen/Veo) transfer across agents and are the most portable investment. For comparison, try OpenAI's Codex CLI, Aider, opencode and Cline to see how the same repository behaves under different agents before committing scripts to one vendor.
